method_card.title: How to Use Powers, Roots and Standard Form
method_card.content:
Powers: \(a^n\) means \(a\) multiplied by itself \(n\) times, so \(3^4 = 3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3 = 81\). Note \(a^0 = 1\).

Roots undo powers: \(\sqrt{196} = 14\) because \(14^2 = 196\), and \(\sqrt[3]{64} = 4\) because \(4^3 = 64\).

Standard form is \(A \times 10^n\) with \(1 \le A < 10\). Slide the point until one digit is in front and count the places: large numbers give a positive \(n\), small numbers a negative \(n\).

Calculating: to multiply, multiply the fronts and add the powers; to divide, divide the fronts and subtract the powers. Adjust \(A\) back into range if needed.
method_card.example:
Write 0.00045 in standard form

Step 1: Move the decimal right until A is between 1 and 10: \(0.00045 \rightarrow 4.5\) (moved 4 places right)

Step 2: Since we moved right (small number), \(n\) is negative: \(n = -4\)

Answer: \(4.5 \times 10^{-4}\)

steps: Negative powers mean small numbers: \(5 \times 10^{-2} = 0.05\). Keep the signs when you add or subtract powers.
To add, first rewrite both numbers with the SAME power, then add the fronts.
Always finish by checking \(A\) is between 1 and 10. If \(0.36 \times 10^5\) is not, adjust it to \(3.6 \times 10^4\).
